Shipping a Ledger Rewrite Without a Freeze

How a small team replaced the storage layer under a live queue, one reader at a time, and never stopped taking writes.

Why the old ledger had to go

The first ledger was a single append-only file that every worker locked in turn. It was simple to reason about and it served for two years, until the queue grew past what one lock could carry.

Three symptoms told us the design had run out of room:

  • Writers waited on the lock longer than they spent writing.
  • A crash mid-append left a torn line the next reader choked on.
  • Compaction needed the whole file in memory at once.

What we measured first

Before touching the format we timed every lock acquisition for a week, so the rewrite would have a number to beat rather than a feeling.

The migration, step by step

We moved readers before writers, because a reader that understands both formats makes every later step reversible.

  1. Teach every reader the new format beside the old one.
  2. Dual-write for a full compaction cycle.
  3. Flip reads to the new format behind a flag.
  4. Stop writing the old format once nothing reads it.

What we would do again

Keeping the old reader alive for a month after the switch cost almost nothing and saved us twice, when a replay needed history the new format had not yet backfilled.
